Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo earlier. A few follow-ups from our side as we scope integration:

- SDK: we run a Java backend (Spring Boot). Do you support a Java SDK or a simple HTTP client with token rotation? Any sample code?
- Auth: we need to decide between API keys, short-lived tokens, or mTLS. Can you confirm what Redwood supports in Private vs Hosted?
- Routing/Region: our primary cluster is in us-east-1; we'd like region pinning and failover to another US region. Latency target P95 ~250ms.
- Fallbacks: for cost control we want a clear fallback chain (low-latency model -> cost model) and a way to keep structured tool-calling consistent across fallbacks.
- Embeddings/rerank: can you outline a recommended pattern for candidate recall + rerank? How are tokens billed for embedding+rerank flows?

Can we schedule a 30-minute technical follow-up with your engineer + our TechOps (cc'd) on Wed 6/16? Also please send any sample config/examples.

Thanks,

Hi Sofia — great to hear from you. Quick recap plus proposed next steps below; attaching a mapping sheet to capture your traffic profile.

High-level answers and next steps:

1) SDK/Auth
- We have first-class SDKs for Python and Node; for Java we provide a maintained HTTP client example and a lightweight token provider helper (attached sample code in the mapping sheet).
- Auth options: Hosted supports API keys and short-lived OAuth tokens. Dedicated/Private supports API keys, short-lived tokens, and mTLS for mutual TLS in Private deployments. We can walk through mTLS setup in the deep-dive.

2) Routing/Region
- You can pin by region using a routing policy (example: prefer us-east-1, failover to us-west-2). Policies are evaluated per-request and include latency thresholds and cost buckets.
- We can set a P95 target for a traffic class and route to lower-latency model variants when P95 exceeds threshold.

3) Fallbacks & Structured output
- Fallback chain is supported. We recommend a primary low-latency quantized model for interactive queries, second-tier cost-optimized quantized model, and a higher-quality model for background/async jobs. Structured tool-calling is preserved across fallbacks by mapping tool schemas; fallback models get the same tool spec so parsing remains stable.

4) Embeddings + rerank
- Pattern: recall with lightweight embeddings (approx 1536-d) -> candidate set -> rerank with an instruct model or dedicated reranker endpoint. Token billing: embeddings generation billed per embedding call; rerank is billed as model tokens for the reranker query.

Proposed next steps:
- Technical deep-dive with Dev (our infra) and your TechOps: Wed 2028-06-16 at 11:00am PDT. Please confirm.
- Dev will prepare a short Java SDK auth guide and a sample routing policy for your traffic profile.
- I attached quantumcare-mapping-sheet.csv to capture throughput, average tokens, and peak windows. I also attached a first-pass SLA draft for your review.

If that sounds good I will lock the calendar and we can get an initial cost estimate after you populate the mapping sheet.

Thanks,

Subject: RE: Post-demo questions: SDK auth, routing, fallbacks

Sofia — quick tech notes ahead of the deep-dive. I took Ben's summary and sketched concrete config you can start with.

Java SDK / Auth example
- We dont ship a full Java binary SDK yet, but our HTTP client pattern is straightforward. Token rotation sample: use a short-lived token endpoint and refresh before expiry. For mTLS we provide cert creation steps for Private customers.

Sample routing policy (YAML)
- traffic_class: interactive
  region_preference: [us-east-1, us-west-2]
  latency_threshold_ms: 300
  fallbacks:
    - model: redwood-llm-lowlat-8q
      priority: 1
    - model: redwood-llm-cost-4q
      priority: 2
    - model: open-7b-quant
      priority: 3

Embedding+rerank pattern
- step 1: call embeddings endpoint for query -> store/compare to vector index
- step 2: recall top-N ids (e.g. 40)
- step 3: batch rerank with a cross-encoder/small instruct model for final sort
- batching: we recommend batching rerank calls in groups of 8-16 to shave cost while keeping latency under target

Notes on token accounting
- Embedding generation billed per embedding request; reranker billed as usual model tokens. If you perform recall+rerank in a single flow (embed -> prompt with candidates) the prompt size will include candidate context tokens. We can help estimate cost once we have average candidate sizes.

Operational items I will prepare for the meeting:
- Java auth guide and token rotation sample
- Routing policy JSON you can drop into your config store
- Short test harness to exercise regional failover and model fallback (includes simple latency simulator)

Ben, Marissa: I can circulate the RFC-style routing policy before Wed.

- Dev

Thanks Ben and Dev — this is helpful. A couple clarifications before the deep-dive:

- Latency: our internal target is P95 <= 250ms for interactive intents. We also have a background worker flow where higher-latency, higher-quality responses are fine.
- Throughput: anticipated steady-state 50 req/s, spikes to 250 req/s for short windows. Avg tokens per request ~80.
- Contractors: we will be bringing two third-party contractors to work on the integration. Can Redwood support contractor accounts with scoped access/audit logs?
- Fallback behavior: we want deterministic structured output even when falling back. If a lower-tier model fails to conform to tool-call schema, we want an automatic escalation to the next model in the chain and a flag in the event payload.

Also: can you provide an estimate ballpark for monthly cost given the mapping sheet assumptions? We can fill the mapping sheet before the meeting but any heuristic helps.

I confirmed Wed 6/16 11:00am PDT works for TechOps.

Best,
Sofia
